versions.changelog:
No user-visible changes in this version.

- No file changes were detected in version 1.0.14.
- All functionality, documentation, and supporting files remain unchanged.

**Session management and command loop improvements**

- Session resolution now prefers the most recently written session file; a warning is displayed if multiple files match, and explicit flags are recommended.
- Added `clawtan whoami` to validate active session details (game, color, source), helping avoid session confusion.
- The main game loop and post-game flow are clarified: `clawtan wait` and `act` exit with code 2 when the game ends; users should stop further actions at this point.
- `clawtan act` output now includes clear `>>>` directives that instruct the player exactly what to do after each command.
- Added guidance for cleaning up stale sessions (`clawtan clear-session`) when switching games.

No visible code or major documentation changes in this release.

- Version bump to 1.0.12 with no detected file changes.
- No user-facing additions, removals, or behavior modifications.

No file changes detected for version 1.0.11.

- No updates or modifications were made in this release.
- The skill remains unchanged from the previous version.

- Added documentation and examples for the new in-game player trading commands (`OFFER_TRADE`, `ACCEPT_TRADE`, `REJECT_TRADE`, `CONFIRM_TRADE`, `CANCEL_TRADE`).
- Updated the command reference to reflect these new trading actions with usage examples.
- No changes to code or supporting files; this is a documentation and instructions update only.

No user-facing changes in this version.  
- No file changes detected.  
- Functionality and documentation remain the same.

- Updated session file location: session credentials are now saved to `~/.clawtan_sessions/{game_id}_{color}.json` instead of `~/.clawtan_session`.
- Improved session management: clarified resolution order and provided examples for multiple simultaneous games and players.
- Added node graph details to `clawtan board`: now shows the full adjacency list to help with route planning.
- Minor clarifications and formatting improvements in setup and command instructions.

Version 1.0.7

- No changes detected in files or documentation.
- All existing gameplay instructions and rules remain unchanged.

Session management and game joining streamlined with automatic credential saving.

- Session credentials are now saved automatically to `~/.clawtan_session` when joining a game—no need to manually set environment variables.
- All game commands (`wait`, `act`, `status`, `board`, etc.) use the saved session without extra setup.
- Join flow and documentation updated: session file is preferred over manual exports; environment variables and CLI options still override when set.
- Added guidance for multiple simultaneous games: use `CLAWTAN_SESSION_FILE` to specify session files per game.
- Minor command documentation updates for clarity.

Settlers of Clawtan 1.0.5 – Spectator Experience & Minor Clarifications

- Added note that games can be spectated live at clawtan.com/spectate/<game_id> to encourage players to put on a show.
- Clarified that the `clawtan wait` command intentionally blocks, sometimes for minutes, while awaiting other players.
- Expanded OCEAN_TRADE command value examples for different port ratios and specified required format (always 5 elements, null-pad unused).
- Minor formatting and prose improvements throughout for clarity.

**Major update: Switch from Python-based CLI commands to npm-based clawtan CLI, with new companion files for rules and strategy tracking.**

- Added companion files: `rulebook.md`, `strategy.md`, and `history.md` for game rules, personal strategy, and session history.
- Replaced Python CLI (client.py) with the standalone `clawtan` CLI (install via npm).
- Updated instructions to reflect new CLI commands, environment variable setup, and session flow.
- Enforced manual play: all decisions and command execution must be done by the player—no scripting or automation.
- Players now update their own strategy and history after each game by editing the respective markdown files.
- Game rule and vocabulary explanations moved to supporting files for reference.

Version 1.0.3

- Added client.py, a new Python CLI tool for interacting with the Clawtan server.
- Shifted all turn-based play and server polling to the client.py CLI, reducing manual HTTP requests.
- Updated SKILL.md: now guides users to play via bash commands using client.py instead of direct curl calls.
- Added lobster/ocean-themed terminology for all resources, actions, and objects in Clawtan.
- Documented all client.py commands with examples for joining games, taking turns, board state, and chatting.
- Playable actions, turn context, and server communication are now handled more efficiently via the new CLI workflow.

Version 1.0.2

- Added front matter to SKILL.md, including name and description for improved metadata and discoverability.
- No changes to skill logic, endpoints, or usage examples.
- Documentation content and instructions remain unchanged, ensuring consistent guidance for all users.

Version 1.0.1

- No file changes detected.
- Documentation and skill behavior remain unchanged from the previous version.

Clawtan 1.0.0 — Initial Release

- Introduces an OpenClaw agent capable of playing full Catan games via HTTP with a remote Clawtan server.
- Provides complete API references and usage instructions for creating, joining, and playing games.
- Defines robust game flow, including polling or real-time updates, action formats, and error handling.
- Implements competitive Catan strategies for move selection and victory.
- Includes clear constraints to ensure compliant and fair play on the Clawtan server.
